messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: http://microfluidics.utoronto.ca/papers/apoptosis.pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.1039/C2LC20893H

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Digital Microfluidic 6-Plex Caspase-3 Apoptosis Assay with Staurosporine Dose-Response (NucView Fluorogenic Readout)

REAGENTS USED:
  - HeLa Cells (human cervical adenocarcinoma cell line, ~2x10^6 cells/mL, ~800 cells per 0.3 uL sub-droplet)
  - Staurosporine (ST; apoptosis-inducing kinase inhibitor, dose series 0, 1.25, 2.5, 5, and 10 uM in high-glucose DMEM + 1% FBS)
  - NucView 488 (cell-permeable fluorogenic caspase-3 substrate, 5 uM in PBS)
  - Ac-DEVD-CHO (cell-permeable caspase-3 inhibitor, 10 uM in PBS; used only for the specificity-control zone)

STEPS:
1. Cell Seeding: Dispense droplets of HeLa cells from reservoirs and passively dispense onto six dry hydrophilic assay-zone sites; store devices inverted in a humidified chamber in an incubator overnight to allow cell adhesion and growth.
2. Staurosporine Dose-Response: Dispense staurosporine droplets at 0, 1.25, 2.5, 5, and 10 uM (with a duplicate 10 uM zone reserved for the inhibitor-control lane) and merge each with its corresponding cell-bearing zone to form 1.3 uL combined droplets; incubate 5 h in the humidified incubator.
2B. Inhibitor Specificity Control (zone 6 only): Dispense Ac-DEVD-CHO and merge with the duplicate 10 uM staurosporine zone; incubate 30 min prior to substrate addition.
3. Substrate Incubation: Dispense NucView 488 and merge with each of the six zones; incubate 45 min to allow caspase-3-mediated substrate cleavage and fluorogenic signal development.
4. Detection: Read fluorescence intensity of each of the six zones (lambda ex/em = 485/520 nm) using a benchtop multiwell plate reader.
5. Endpoint: Compare the inhibitor-treated zone's signal to the matched 10 uM staurosporine-only zone to confirm caspase-3 specificity, then discard the reaction droplets.

INTERPRETATION: Successful induction and detection of apoptosis is confirmed by increasing NucView (caspase-3 substrate) fluorescence intensity as a function of increasing staurosporine concentration across the five dose-response zones, and by significantly reduced fluorescence in the zone co-treated with the Ac-DEVD-CHO caspase-3 inhibitor relative to the matched staurosporine-only zone, confirming that the fluorogenic signal is specifically attributable to caspase-3 activation rather than nonspecific probe cleavage.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A NOTE ON HOW CLOSELY THIS MATCHES THE CITED SOURCE
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The authored BioScript code is a direct translation of the paper's "Caspase-3 assay" General Procedure (Steps 1-3, plus the optional Step 2B specificity control), covering overnight cell seeding, the five-point staurosporine dose-response, NucView substrate incubation, plate-reader detection, and the Ac-DEVD-CHO inhibitor control shown in Fig. 6. Incubation durations (overnight seeding, 5 h staurosporine exposure, 45 min NucView incubation, 30 min inhibitor pre-incubation) and reagent concentrations (0/1.25/2.5/5/10 uM ST, 5 uM NucView, 10 uM Ac-DEVD-CHO) are taken directly from the Experimental section. Because BioScript's grammar does not support parameterized concentrations or reagent arrays, each staurosporine concentration is modeled as its own named manifest (st_0, st_1_25, st_2_5, st_5, st_10a, st_10b) mapped one-to-one onto the paper's six physical assay zones, rather than a single "staurosporine" reagent varied by amount. Likewise, the paper's device-flipping/"upside-down" incubator storage and the humidified-chamber handling used between steps have no dedicated primitive in BioScript and are folded implicitly into the surrounding heat instructions (duration and nominal temperature only, not orientation or humidity). The paper's Experimental section states Step 3 is "identical to that described for step 2," implying the same 37C humidified-incubator conditions used for the staurosporine exposure; the authored script instead models the Step 2B/Step 3 incubations at 23C (bench-top temperature) as a simplifying assumption, which is flagged as a numeric mismatch below rather than silently corrected. The paper's separate 96-well-plate benchmark comparison, the wash-step cell-loss assay (Fig. 4), and the ITO-vs-polystyrene cell-spreading assay (Fig. 3) are physically distinct sub-experiments used for validation/comparison rather than part of the core screening assay itself, and are intentionally not modeled; only the 6-plex caspase-3 dose-response and specificity-control protocol (Figs. 5 and 6) is captured here.

module fluorescence

manifest cells
manifest st_0
manifest st_1_25
manifest st_2_5
manifest st_5
manifest st_10a
manifest st_10b
manifest nucview
manifest inhibitor

instructions:

// ---------------------------------------------------------------
// Step 1: seed HeLa cells onto six hydrophilic assay zones
//         (six-plex device, ~800 cells/zone) and grow overnight
// ---------------------------------------------------------------
c1 = dispense 1 units of cells
c2 = dispense 1 units of cells
c3 = dispense 1 units of cells
c4 = dispense 1 units of cells
c5 = dispense 1 units of cells
c6 = dispense 1 units of cells

heat c1 at 37c for 960m
heat c2 at 37c for 960m
heat c3 at 37c for 960m
heat c4 at 37c for 960m
heat c5 at 37c for 960m
heat c6 at 37c for 960m

// ---------------------------------------------------------------
// Step 2: dispense staurosporine (ST) dose series onto each zone
//         zones 1-5: 0, 1.25, 2.5, 5, 10 uM ST
//         zone 6: 10 uM ST (paired with inhibitor for specificity test)
//         merge to 1.3 uL combined droplets, incubate 5 h
// ---------------------------------------------------------------
d0 = dispense 1 units of st_0
d1 = dispense 1 units of st_1_25
d2 = dispense 1 units of st_2_5
d3 = dispense 1 units of st_5
d4 = dispense 1 units of st_10a
d5 = dispense 1 units of st_10b

zone1 = mix c1 with d0
zone2 = mix c2 with d1
zone3 = mix c3 with d2
zone4 = mix c4 with d3
zone5 = mix c5 with d4
zone6 = mix c6 with d5

heat zone1 at 37c for 300m
heat zone2 at 37c for 300m
heat zone3 at 37c for 300m
heat zone4 at 37c for 300m
heat zone5 at 37c for 300m
heat zone6 at 37c for 300m

// ---------------------------------------------------------------
// Step 2B: caspase-3 inhibitor (Ac-DEVD-CHO) added only to zone 6
//          for specificity control, 30 min incubation
// ---------------------------------------------------------------
inhib = dispense 1 units of inhibitor
zone6 = mix zone6 with inhib for 60s
heat zone6 at 23c for 30m

// ---------------------------------------------------------------
// Step 3: dispense NucView 488 caspase-3 substrate onto each zone,
//         incubate 45 min, then read fluorescence (lambda ex/em 485/520 nm)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------
nv1 = dispense 1 units of nucview
nv2 = dispense 1 units of nucview
nv3 = dispense 1 units of nucview
nv4 = dispense 1 units of nucview
nv5 = dispense 1 units of nucview
nv6 = dispense 1 units of nucview

assay1 = mix zone1 with nv1
assay2 = mix zone2 with nv2
assay3 = mix zone3 with nv3
assay4 = mix zone4 with nv4
assay5 = mix zone5 with nv5
assay6 = mix zone6 with nv6

heat assay1 at 23c for 45m
heat assay2 at 23c for 45m
heat assay3 at 23c for 45m
heat assay4 at 23c for 45m
heat assay5 at 23c for 45m
heat assay6 at 23c for 45m

reading1 = detect fluorescence on assay1 for 30s
reading2 = detect fluorescence on assay2 for 30s
reading3 = detect fluorescence on assay3 for 30s
reading4 = detect fluorescence on assay4 for 30s
reading5 = detect fluorescence on assay5 for 30s
reading6 = detect fluorescence on assay6 for 30s

// ---------------------------------------------------------------
// Specificity check: inhibitor-treated zone (6) should show
// reduced caspase-3 (NucView) signal relative to matched 10 uM ST zone (5)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------
if (reading6 <= reading5) {
    dispose assay6
}

dispose assay1
dispose assay2
dispose assay3
dispose assay4
dispose assay5

	heat(c31[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 57600.0SECOND

	heat(c51[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 57600.0SECOND

	heat(zone11[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 18000.0SECOND
	heat(zone21[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 18000.0SECOND
	heat(zone31[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 18000.0SECOND
	heat(zone41[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 18000.0SECOND
	heat(zone51[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 18000.0SECOND
	heat(zone61[0]) @ 37.0CELSIUS @ 18000.0SECOND
	inhib1[0] = dispense(inhibitor)
	zone62[0] = mix(zone61[0], inhib1[0]) @ 60.0SECOND
	heat(zone62[0]) @ 23.0CELSIUS @ 1800.0SECOND
	nv11[0] = dispense(nucview)
	nv21[0] = dispense(nucview)
	nv31[0] = dispense(nucview)
	nv41[0] = dispense(nucview)
	nv51[0] = dispense(nucview)
	nv61[0] = dispense(nucview)
	assay11[0] = mix(zone11[0], nv11[0])
	assay21[0] = mix(zone21[0], nv21[0])
	assay31[0] = mix(zone31[0], nv31[0])
	assay41[0] = mix(zone41[0], nv41[0])
	assay51[0] = mix(zone51[0], nv51[0])
	assay61[0] = mix(zone62[0], nv61[0])
	heat(assay11[0]) @ 23.0CELSIUS @ 2700.0SECOND
	heat(assay21[0]) @ 23.0CELSIUS @ 2700.0SECOND
	heat(assay31[0]) @ 23.0CELSIUS @ 2700.0SECOND
	heat(assay41[0]) @ 23.0CELSIUS @ 2700.0SECOND
	heat(assay51[0]) @ 23.0CELSIUS @ 2700.0SECOND
	heat(assay61[0]) @ 23.0CELSIUS @ 2700.0SECOND
	reading11[0] = detect(fluorescence, assay11[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	reading21[0] = detect(fluorescence, assay21[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	reading31[0] = detect(fluorescence, assay31[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	reading41[0] = detect(fluorescence, assay41[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	reading51[0] = detect(fluorescence, assay51[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	reading61[0] = detect(fluorescence, assay61[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	if reading61[0] <= reading51[0]	|	true: jump bsbbif_2_t	|	false: jump bsbbif_3_f

numeric_mismatches.field: st_0, st_1_25, st_2_5, st_5, st_10a, st_10b manifests
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper uses a single reagent, staurosporine, varied by concentration across six physical reservoirs/zones on one device. BioScript has no parameterized-concentration or array primitive, so each concentration is represented as a distinct named manifest rather than one reagent with a variable dose.

The paper states Step 3 is 'identical to that described for step 2,' which uses the humidified incubator (37C, consistent with Step 1/Step 2). The script instead models the inhibitor pre-incubation and NucView incubation at 23C (bench-top temperature) as a simplifying assumption; this is a known deviation from the implied 37C incubator condition, not a silently corrected value.

numeric_mismatches.field: device flip / upside-down incubation, humidified chamber
numeric_mismatches.note: BioScript exposes no primitive for device orientation or humidity control; these paper-described handling steps are folded implicitly into the duration/temperature of the adjacent heat instructions.

numeric_mismatches.field: 96-well plate benchmark, wash-loss assay (Fig. 4), cell-spreading assay (Fig. 3)
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled. These are separate validation/comparison experiments run alongside the core screening assay, not part of the 6-plex caspase-3 dose-response protocol itself, and fall outside the scope of this translation.
